φησὶν, ἴδεν, ὑποκει- μένων τῶν Σαραφείμ· ἐπὶ θρόνου δὲ ἄνθρωπον τε- θεᾶσθαι,
ἤτοι εἶδος ἀνθρώπου, οὗ τὰ μὲν ἄνω φησὶν ἠλέκτρῳ προσεοικέναι, τό γε μὴν ἐξ
ὀσφύος εἰς πόδας ὡς ὅρασις πυρός. Ἑκάστῃ δὲ τῶν τοιούτων ὁράσεων, ἔμφασίν
τινα δόξης τῆς θεοπρεποῦς, καὶ μυστηρίου τοῦ κατὰ Χριστὸν, ἀστείως ἡμῖν
ὑπαινίττεται. Οὐδὲν οὖν ἄρα τὸ κωλύον κἀν τούτῳ νοεῖν, ἐπὶ νεφέλης κούφης
τεθεᾶσθαι τὸν Κύριον, χρειωδέστατά τε καὶ ἀναγκαίως. Ἀποπληροῖ γὰρ ἡμῖν ἡ
νεφέλη τύπον ὑετοῦ τε καὶ δρόσου πνευματικῆς, καὶ αὐτοῦ δὲ τοῦ σωτηρίου
βαπτίσματος. Καὶ γοῦν ὁ μακάριος Παῦλος, τοὺς ἐξ αἵματος Ἰσραὴλ βεβαπτίσθαι
φησὶν ἐν τῇ νε- φέλῃ καὶ ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ· ἐπήρτητο καὶ τὴν βαθεῖαν ἐκείνην
διαπεραιουμένοις ἔρημον, ἐν ἡμέρᾳ μὲν ἡ νεφέλη· προηγεῖτο δὲ καὶ νυκτὶ στύλος
πυρός. Ἐγρά- 70.453 φετο δὲ δι' ἀμφοῖν ὁ Χριστὸς, ἤτοι τὸ ἐπ' αὐτῷ μυ- στήριον,
ἤγουν ὡς ἐν πίστει τε καὶ ἁγίῳ βαπτίσματι, δικαίωσις καὶ ἁγιασμός. Ἔδει τοίνυν ἐπὶ
καθάρσει τε καὶ μεταβολῇ ἰόντα τὸν Κύριον τῶν Αἰγυπτίων, θεοπρεπῶς δὲ
δηλονότι καὶ νοητῶς, ἐπὶ νεφέλης ὁρᾶ- σθαι κούφης. Οὐ γὰρ ἦν ἑτέρως
ἀποσμήχεσθαι τῆς τῶν πλανωμένων ψυχῆς τὴν ἐντετηγμένην αὐτῇ κη- λῖδα, μὴ
οὐχὶ διὰ τοῦ ἁγίου βαπτίσματος. Οὗ καὶ εἰς τύπον τὴν νεφέλην εἶναι διοριζόμεθα.
Κούφη δὲ ἡ νεφέλη καὶ μάλα εἰκότως ὠνόμασται. Βαπτιζόμεθα γὰρ εἰς ἀπόθεσιν
ἁμαρτίας, καὶ οἱονεί τι δυσδιακό- μιστον ἀληθῶς φορτίον ἀποτρεπόμενοι τὴν
ἀσέβειαν, ὑπόπτεροι τρόπον τινὰ διὰ τούτου γινόμεθα, καὶ τὰ ἄνω φρονεῖν, καὶ τὰς
καρδίας ἔχειν ὑψοῦ μανθάνομεν. Τό γε μὴν ἐπικαθῆσθαι τῇ νεφέλῃ τὸν Κύριον,
ἐκεῖνο οἶμαι δηλοῦν· Ἡ κάθησις ἢ ἀνάπαυσιν, ἤγουν ἐξου- σίαν ἡμῖν ὑπαινίττεται.
Οὐκοῦν ἐπαναπαύεται Χρι- στὸς, οὐχὶ τῇ κατὰ νόμον λατρείᾳ ποθὲν, ἐν τελειώσει δὲ
μᾶλλον τῇ διὰ τοῦ ἁγίου βαπτίσματος. Βεβασί- λευκε δὲ οὕτω τῶν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς.
Σεισθήσεσθαι δέ φησι τὰ χειροποίητα Αἰγύπτου ἀπὸ προσώπου αὐτοῦ. Ἀνα-
δεδειγμένου γὰρ ἤδη τοῦ ἁγίου βαπτίσματος, καὶ Χρι- στοῦ λοιπὸν ἐπιλάμψαντος,
πᾶσά πως ἀνάγκη, τὰ τῆς ἀρχαίας ἀπάτης ἀφανίζεσθαι παίγνια, καὶ τὰς τοῦ
διαβόλου παγίδας ὁρᾶσθαι συντεθραυσμένας. Σε- σαγήνευκε δὲ πρὸς ὄλεθρον καὶ
ἀπώλειαν ἅπαν μὲν, ὡς ἔπος εἰπεῖν, ἔθνος τε καὶ γένος, μάλιστα δὲ τῶν ἄλλων τοὺς
Αἰγυπτίους. ∆εισιδαιμονέστατοι γὰρ γε- γόνασι παρὰ τοὺς ἄλλους, καὶ τάχα που
νικῶντες ἐν πλάνῃ Πέρσας τε καὶ Ἀσσυρίους· καίτοι τῆς θεο- πνεύστου Γραφῆς περὶ
τῆς ἐκείνων λεγούσης χώρας, ὅτι γῆ γλυπτῶν ἐστιν. Ἡττηθήσεσθαι δὲ τὴν καρδίαν
τῶν Αἰγυπτίων φησὶν, παραχωρήσασαν, ὥς γε οἶμαι
pass_a_gloss: [...] of man coming with the clouds, and he has set the things next to these in order. And Ezekiel likewise saw, he says, a firmament, the seraphim lying beneath; and on a throne to have beheld a man, or the form of a man, whose upper parts he says resembled amber, and the part from the loin to feet as an appearance of fire. And in each of such visions he elegantly hints to us some image of the glory befitting God, and of the mystery concerning Christ. Nothing then is the hindrance to understanding in this too that the Lord was beheld on a light cloud, most usefully and necessarily. For the cloud fills out for us a type of spiritual rain and dew, and of the saving baptism itself. And indeed the blessed Paul says that those from the blood of Israel were baptized in the cloud and in the sea; and over those crossing that deep desert hung by day the cloud; and by night a pillar of fire led before. And through both Christ was being written, that is, the mystery concerning him, namely, as in faith and holy baptism, justification and sanctification. It was needed then that the Lord, going for cleansing and change of the Egyptians, in a way befitting God clearly and spiritually, should be seen on a light cloud. For it was not possible otherwise to wipe off from the soul of those who stray the stain melted into it, except through the holy baptism. Of which also we define the cloud to be for a type. And the cloud has very fittingly been named light. For we are baptized for the putting off of sin, and as if turning away ungodliness, truly a burden hard to carry, we become in a certain way winged through this, and we learn to think the things above, and to have the hearts on high. And as for the Lord's sitting upon the cloud, I think it shows that: the sitting hints to us either rest or authority. So Christ rests, not on the worship according to the Law anywhere, but rather in the perfecting through the holy baptism. And thus he has reigned over those on the earth. And he says the handmade things of Egypt will be shaken from before his face. For holy baptism having already been shown forth, and Christ at last having shone upon [them], it is in every way necessary that the playthings of the ancient deceit be made to vanish, and that the snares of the devil be seen shattered. And he had netted for ruin and destruction every, so to speak, nation and race, but most of all the others the Egyptians. For they became most superstitious beside the others, and perhaps conquering in error Persians and Assyrians; although the God-inspired Scripture says about the country of those that it is a land of carved images. And he says the heart of the Egyptians will be defeated, giving way, as I think [the section breaks off].
pass_b_english: …coming with the clouds (Daniel 7:13), and he set down what follows. Ezekiel likewise says that he saw a firmament with the seraphim beneath it, and on the throne he saw a man, or rather the likeness of a man, whose upper parts, he says, resembled amber, while from the loins to the feet he was like the appearance of fire (Ezekiel 1:22–27).

In each of these visions he subtly hints to us at an image of the glory that befits God and of the mystery of Christ. Nothing, then, prevents us from understanding that here too the Lord was seen on a light cloud for a most useful and necessary purpose. For the cloud fills out for us a type of spiritual rain and dew, and of saving baptism itself.

Indeed, the blessed Paul says that those of Israel's blood were baptized in the cloud and in the sea (1 Corinthians 10:2). As they crossed that deep desert, the cloud hung over them by day, and by night a pillar of fire went before them (Exodus 13:21). Through both of these Christ was being portrayed, that is, the mystery concerning him: justification and sanctification in faith and holy baptism.

So the Lord, coming to cleanse and transform the Egyptians, in a manner fitting God and spiritually, of course, had to be seen on a light cloud. For there was no other way to scrub from the soul of those in error the stain ingrained in it except through holy baptism; and we hold that the cloud is a type of that baptism.

And the cloud is very fittingly called light. For we are baptized for the putting away of sin; and as we turn away from ungodliness as from a burden truly hard to carry, we become, in a way, winged by this, and learn to set our minds on things above (Colossians 3:2) and to keep our hearts on high.

As for the Lord's sitting upon the cloud, I think it shows this: sitting hints to us at either rest or authority. So Christ rests, not in any way in worship according to the law, but rather in the perfection that comes through holy baptism; and in this way he has come to reign over those on earth.

He says that the handmade things of Egypt will be shaken before his face (Isaiah 19:1). For once holy baptism had been revealed and Christ had shone forth, it was wholly necessary that the playthings of the ancient deceit should vanish and the snares of the devil be seen broken to pieces.

For the devil had caught in his net, for ruin and destruction, practically every nation and race, but the Egyptians more than the rest. They were the most superstitious of all, perhaps outdoing even the Persians and Assyrians in error, although the God-inspired Scripture says of those peoples' land that it is a land of carved images (Jeremiah 50:38).
He says that the heart of the Egyptians will be overcome, yielding, as I think…

choices.why: Cyril names the seraphim beneath Ezekiel's firmament; the English follows his wording though Ezekiel 1 speaks of living creatures.
κηλίς is a stain or blot to be scrubbed away by baptism.

choices.english: Through both of these Christ was being portrayed
choices.why: ἐγράφετο (split in print by a column number) is used of a figure drawn beforehand, a type.
The light cloud becomes a picture of the baptized lifted from the weight of sin.
Cyril explains sitting as either rest or authority; both are kept.
